entries.title: Requirements of Crew - Immigration
entries.text: Immigration procedures flight crews must follow when departing and arriving at RAK Airport.

entries.title: On Departure
entries.text: All operating crew must be physically present. Crew submit their Identity Cards with flight details; Airport Ground Services prepares a General Declaration (GD), which is stamped and submitted to Immigration with the arrival GD.

entries.title: On Arrival
entries.text: Flight crew present the arrival GD and Identity Cards to Immigration to obtain crew clearance.

entries.title: No Alterations
entries.text: No corrections, alterations or overwriting are allowed on the GD, which must show correct routing and dates.

entries.title: Exit Stamps
entries.text: Exit stamps from the origin station’s Immigration must appear on the GD. Military airport origins require an Operations Department stamp instead.

entries.title: Carry Valid ID
entries.text: A valid company ID must be carried at all times. Crew complete immigration together unless prior notice is given for those staying back or arriving early.

entries.title: Airside Driving License
entries.text: Any vehicle operator in airside areas must hold a valid Airport Driving Permit (ADP) issued by the PRO.

entries.title: Photo & Licence
entries.text: One passport-sized photograph and a copy of a valid UAE/GCC driving licence or police-issued airport driving licence.

entries.title: Forms
entries.text: A completed ADP Application Form and a company letter stating the payment method.

entries.title: Renewals
entries.text: For renewals, include a photocopy of the existing ADP. Renewing before expiry is the permit holder’s responsibility.

entries.title: Rules for permit holders
entries.text: Drivers must carry their current permit at all times in airside areas. Companies are responsible for ensuring staff hold valid public driving licences, and equipment-specific training must be certified to Apron Services in advance.. Carry your permit at all times airside. Return the ADP when no longer driving. Equipment training certified in advance

entries.title: Steps for shippers
entries.text: To export freight out of RAK International Airport, the shipper should:. Obtain an export code from RAK Customs office. Fill in the Shipper’s Letter of Instruction (provided by the export office). Complete customs formalities - via an authorised clearing agent. Provide a copy of the invoice to prove the value to customs. The air waybill is held by the handling agent

entries.title: Other requirements
entries.text: Documents vary by cargo type:. General Cargo: invoice & packing list. Live Animal Cargo: import permit from MOCCAE. Perishable Cargo: Ministry of Agriculture certificate. Valuable Cargo: invoice & insurance policy. Unaccompanied Baggage: passport copy & declaration of value. Human Remains: death & embalming certificates, police & consulate clearance, cancelled passport, ticket details

entries.title: Clearing imports
entries.text: To clear an import freight at RAK International Airport:. Clear the shipment through an authorised agent. Obtain an Importer Code & Customs Clearance ID Card from RAK Customs Main Office

entries.title: Required documents
entries.text: The Customs Department requires:. General Cargo: original invoice, packing list & certificate of origin. Live Animal Cargo: import permit from MOCCAE. Perishable Cargo: health certificate, certificate of origin, original invoice & packing list

entries.title: Luggage & Check-In
entries.text: Know what you can carry so you can pack smart and breeze through security.

entries.title: Liquids in cabin bags
entries.text: Place liquids, aerosols and gels in one transparent, resealable bag. Individual containers must be 100 ml or less, with a total capacity of no more than one litre.. Medication and baby food may be exempt. Keep the bag easy to remove at security

entries.title: Checked Baggage
entries.text: Baggage allowances and restrictions vary by airline and destination. Passengers are advised to check with their airline before travelling to confirm baggage allowance, fees, and restrictions.. Check excess-baggage fees with your airline. Allow extra time for oversized bags

entries.title: Electronics & batteries
entries.text: Keep laptops, tablets and power banks in your hand luggage, where they are easy to reach. At security, place larger electronics in a separate tray.. Power banks belong in cabin baggage. Do not pack restricted batteries in checked bags

entries.title: Remove old tags
entries.text: Take off labels and tags from previous trips so baggage scanners can read the current journey correctly.

entries.title: Secure loose straps
entries.text: Fasten or tuck away straps and handles so they do not catch in the baggage-handling system.

entries.title: Prepare backpacks
entries.text: Zip backpacks securely and tuck in every strap before check-in to keep them compact and protected.

entries.title: Choose the right shape
entries.text: Avoid overfilled or irregularly shaped bags. Structured baggage with at least one flat surface is easier to process.

entries.title: Baggage rules to remember
entries.text: Oversized baggage, including bags longer than 90 cm, higher than 75 cm or wider than 60 cm, should be checked at your airline counter and then taken to the oversized-baggage counter. Security may inspect checked bags and remove prohibited or suspicious items when required.. Keep e-cigarettes, fuel cells and motorised devices out of checked baggage. Strong, good-quality cardboard boxes can be accepted as checked baggage. Travel insurance is recommended for extra peace of mind

entries.title: Baggage wrapping
entries.text: Secure wrapping is available in the check-in area. Weigh your bags before wrapping to help avoid unnecessary delays.

entries.title: Careers
entries.text: Build your future with one of the UAE’s fastest-growing airports.

entries.title: Current Openings
entries.text: Browse our current vacancies and apply online.

entries.title: Apply for an Internship
entries.text: Send your CV to careers@rakairport.com with the subject “Internship application”.

entries.title: Student Internship
entries.text: A three-to-six-month training term to gain basic knowledge and experience in your field of study; it can count towards a university graduation requirement.. Request letter from the university. Must be enrolled in a college/university program. Minimum GPA of 3.00 from an accredited UAE institute. Able to commit to the full internship period

entries.title: Graduate Internship
entries.text: A six-month to one-year full-time on-the-job programme across departments such as IT, Procurement, Finance, HR, Electronics, Projects & Engineering, Commercial, Ground Handling, Operations, Safety, Security, Quality and Cargo.. Age group 18–30. Certificate, Diploma or Degree from an accredited institute. Fluency in verbal & written English. Willing to learn and adapt to new working situations

entries.title: Performance & placement
entries.text: An intern’s performance is monitored throughout the programme by section managers through written reports and presentations, and on their ability to work individually and as part of a team. On completion, interns are evaluated by managers and HR - those with high competence and outstanding performance are considered for placement opportunities with RAK Airport.. Monitored by section managers. Final evaluation by managers & HR. Top performers considered for placement

entries.title: We never ask for money
entries.text: Ras Al Khaimah International Airport will never ask for money (in any form) from an applicant.

entries.title: In-person interviews
entries.text: We do not make job offers without conducting an in-person interview at our office at Ras Al Khaimah International Airport.

entries.title: No bank details
entries.text: We never ask for any bank account details prior to employment.

entries.title: Official emails only
entries.text: All authorised email communications come from a Ras Al Khaimah International Airport HR account.
